headline: Australia's Home Affairs department says replacing the government's ageing computer systems, which AI could make easier to attack, could cost roughly 15 to 17 billion dollars.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the conference was on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, before the window, and the figure is one official's rough estimate.
importance_line: Public servants and everyone who relies on Australian government services face years of system replacement paid from existing budgets, but the cost is one official's rough estimate with no new funding announced.
summary: The Canberra Times reports that Hamish Hansford, a senior Australian Home Affairs official, told a government security conference in Canberra on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 that replacing the government's old computer systems, which he said AI can help attackers probe "in record time", is a "defining challenge" costing roughly $15 to $17 billion. Another official, Craig Bickell, said departments must pay for it from their existing budgets, and a directive issued the week before requires them to tell Home Affairs by December how they will protect critical systems and which old ones they will retire, and by when.
notes: Read in full. The article gives only the weekday ('Wednesday'); 7 Oct 2026 is inferred from its 11 Oct (UTC) publication. The dollar currency is not stated in the article.
